target_definition.metric: United States two-year Treasury yield monthly change

graph_diagnosis.summary: Inflation, policy guidance, and activity resilience form competing short-rate repricing mechanisms.
weaknesses: Several activity and communication anchors occurred after the case cutoff and require fresh verification.
The graph has no direct yield observation, so the policy-to-yield bridge is weak.
The post-period market commentary cannot establish the historical monthly move.

search_factors.why_search: Inflation persistence changes expected policy easing or tightening.
Policy communication can reset expected short-rate paths.
Rate futures and Treasury curves reveal how guidance is being repriced.
Resilient growth or labor conditions can delay expected easing.
Speeches can qualify how quickly inflation progress permits easing.

checkpoints.mechanism: Sustained disinflation can create room for an easier expected policy path.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Check inflation breadth, services persistence, and revisions in current releases.

checkpoints.mechanism: Guidance toward a less restrictive path can lower expected future short rates.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Compare current statements, projections, and dissent with prior guidance.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Officials emphasize restrictive policy for longer or revise projections upward.

checkpoints.mechanism: Short-dated rate pricing transmits policy expectations into the two-year sector.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Compare futures-implied policy paths, front-end yields, and option-implied uncertainty.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: The curve moves independently of repriced policy expectations.

checkpoints.mechanism: Stronger activity or labor conditions can postpone easing expectations and support short yields.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Verify timely growth, labor, consumption, and inflation data before using this signal.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Activity or labor data weaken materially while inflation continues to cool.

checkpoints.mechanism: Two-year yields reflect the net repricing of expected policy, inflation, and near-term activity.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Reconcile front-end yields with policy guidance, inflation data, and activity surprises.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Yield moves persist without support from policy expectations or macro surprises.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Cooling inflation can support easier guidance, which lowers short-rate expectations when markets accept the path.
applicability_conditions: Policy guidance and futures pricing align.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Resilient activity can delay expected easing and counter a disinflation-driven decline in short yields.
applicability_conditions: Activity and labor data remain firm.
Inflation progress is insufficient for easing.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Inflation improvement dominates and validates an easier expected policy path.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Inflation measures cool broadly and futures price more easing after policy communication.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Resilient activity dominates and pushes expected easing later.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Growth and labor data outperform while front-end futures remove easing expectations.

forecast_audit_questions: Are all policy, inflation, activity, and labor observations available before the forecast cutoff?
Do futures-implied policy expectations agree with current two-year yield moves?
Is inflation progress broad enough to outweigh resilient activity?
Could a policy speech change timing expectations without altering the underlying inflation trend?
